input.line: Audited ratelimit/limiter.js: core fixed-window algorithm (per-key, at most `limit` per `windowMs`, window resets) is correct and matches limiter.test.js. Two findings: (1) buckets Map has no eviction/TTL — unbounded memory growth for high-cardinality keys over long-running processes; (2) limiter state is in-process/in-memory only, so any horizontal scaling needed to sustain 5k rps (multiple Node processes/pods) gives each instance an independent Map, making the effective per-key limit `limit * N_instances` rather than the stated global `limit`. The staging test's "zero false rejections" at 5k rps does not confirm correct per-key enforcement — it is equally consistent with the limit being under-enforced due to traffic being spread across instances. Routing both findings to a repair task.

input.reason: Audit of ratelimit/limiter.js found the core fixed-window algorithm correct, but surfaced two real findings that require code/doc changes rather than just a report: unbounded bucket growth (no eviction) and an in-process-only state model that breaks the stated per-key guarantee once the service scales horizontally (needed to sustain the 5k rps staging load). These are fixes, not review work, so routing to a repair task on the worker who authored the module.

children.title: Fix ratelimit limiter memory leak and document multi-instance limitation
children.purpose: Address two audit findings in ratelimit/limiter.js: (1) the `buckets` Map never evicts entries, so per-key state grows unbounded over the life of a long-running process, especially with high-cardinality keys (e.g. per-IP/per-user) as seen under sustained load (5k rps for 10 min in staging). (2) The limiter's state is a single in-process Map with no cross-process/cross-instance coordination. Any deployment that scales horizontally to sustain meaningful throughput (multiple Node processes, pods, or cluster workers behind a load balancer) will run one independent Map per instance, so the *effective* per-key limit becomes `limit * N_instances` instead of the documented global `limit` per `windowMs`. The staging load test's 'zero false rejections' result at 5k rps does not validate correct enforcement under this topology — it is equally consistent with the limit being silently under-enforced because traffic for any given key rarely concentrated on a single instance long enough to hit the local cap.
children.completion_criteria: limiter.js adds eviction/cleanup for stale buckets (e.g. lazy cleanup on access plus a bound or periodic sweep) so memory does not grow unbounded with key cardinality over time, with a test covering eviction behavior. Additionally, the module's header comment/docs are updated to explicitly state the limiter enforces its limit per-process only (no cross-instance coordination), and to note that horizontal scaling multiplies the effective global limit by the instance count — with a pointer toward a shared-store (e.g. Redis) based approach if a true global limit across instances is required. All existing and new tests in ratelimit/limiter.test.js pass.
